Questions & answers

FAQ & Contact

Most questions answered below. Anything else — just ask.

Getting started

Do I need to be a member to attend a gathering?

No — your first gathering is always free, no membership required. We want you to try it before you commit. After that, you'll need a membership to RSVP to future events. Memberships start at $8/month.

How do I know if I live in the neighborhood?

Common Table centers on the Portsmith District, roughly bounded by River Road to the west, Oak Street to the north, Highway 9 to the east, and the park to the south. If you're close enough to get here by foot or bike, you're in. If you live just outside those edges and feel a pull toward the community, reach out — we make exceptions for good people.

Can I join if I don't know how to cook?

Absolutely. Potlucks welcome store-bought contributions, wine, and excellent cheese. Skill shares are specifically designed for beginners. The only cooking requirement is genuine interest, and even that we can negotiate.

Is Common Table a nonprofit?

We're an informal membership collective — not legally incorporated. Membership fees cover printing, event supplies, the seed library, and the occasional rental of the Common Kitchen. Rosa, Declan, and Priya are all volunteers. There's no profit here; there's just the community.

Gatherings

How often do gatherings happen?

We run 4–6 gatherings per month across all types — potlucks, skill shares, reading circles, and volunteer days. The rhythm varies by season: summer is busiest, winter is quieter and cozier. The monthly newsletter always has the full calendar.

Where do gatherings take place?

All over the neighborhood. Members host in their homes and backyards, we use the Portsmith Branch Library reading room, the Elm Street Community Garden, Riverside Park Pavilion, and the Common Kitchen at 48 Elm Street. Location is always listed clearly on each event.

Can I bring my kids? My dog?

Yes to both, with a small asterisk. Outdoor events (potlucks, volunteer days, garden walks) are always child and dog-friendly. Indoor skill shares and reading circles may have space limitations — check the event details or email us. When in doubt: ask. We almost always say yes.

Can I RSVP for a friend who isn't a member?

Regular and Steward members can bring unlimited guests. Neighbor members can bring one guest per month. Just let us know ahead of time so we have enough chairs (and food).

Hosting your own gathering

What does "host your own gathering" actually mean?

As a Regular or Steward member, you can pitch any gathering you want to run — a cooking class, a repair café, a film screening, a board game afternoon, a neighborhood walk. We help you pick a date, promote it through the newsletter and member channels, and provide logistical support. You bring the expertise and enthusiasm; we bring the rest.

Do I need a space? Equipment?

Not necessarily. We can help arrange the Common Kitchen, the library reading room, or an outdoor space in the park. We also have a small supply closet with folding tables, chairs, a portable speaker, and basic kitchen equipment available for member use. Just give us two weeks' notice.

Membership & payment

How does payment work?

We keep it low-tech. After you submit the join form, Rosa will email you to confirm and set up payment — typically via Venmo, PayPal, or a check dropped off at 48 Elm Street. We don't process cards online and we never store your financial information.

Can I cancel my membership?

Yes, any time, no questions asked. Just send an email to hello@commontable.club and we'll cancel your membership effective at the end of your current billing month. We'll also miss you and probably invite you back next season.

Do you offer reduced or sliding-scale memberships?

Yes. We don't advertise this widely because we don't want to make anyone feel singled out, but we believe cost should never be the reason someone can't be part of this community. Reach out to Rosa directly at hello@commontable.club and we'll work something out quietly.

Can I upgrade or downgrade my tier?

Of course. Just email us and it'll take effect the following month. Many members start as Neighbor and move to Regular once they realize how much they want to host their own gathering. It happens quickly.

Prefer to drop by?

Declan is usually at the Common Kitchen (48 Elm Street) Tuesday and Thursday mornings from 9–11 AM. Walk in, pull up a chair, have a coffee.
